newsitem.title: USA: Oil price spike seen erasing Alaska budget gap.
newsitem.headline: Oil price spike seen erasing Alaska budget gap.

text.p: The recent rise in oil prices is now expected to erase the $400 million gap that once loomed over Alaska's treasury, state officials said Friday.

With oil prices exceeding $20 a barrel -- compared to the $16.75 forecast when the fiscal year budget was passed in May -- the state will reap $428 million more than expected, according to a new state Department of Revenue estimate.
When they passed the $2.4 billion budget for fiscal year 1997, state lawmakers had expected to tap a special savings account to fill the budget gap.
Alaska's fiscal year runs from July 1 to June 30. The state gets about 80 percent of its revenues from oil royalties, taxes and other fees.
Despite the good news for the state's budget, Gov. Tony Knowles said he intends to stick to his plan of reducing the state budget by $100 million over three years.
"While some may be tempted by a temporary increase in revenues, the prudent course is to hold the line and that's exactly what I intend to do," Knowles, a Democrat, said in a news release.
